comparisons.peer_topic: Automotive Market Trends and Product Qualifications
comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for automotive memory is driven by autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), and in-vehicle infotainment. In 2024, the company qualified automotive LPDDR5X, UFS 3.1, and NOR flash solutions for cloud-connected platforms designed for power data-rich, intelligent automotive services.
comparisons.comparison: QCOM and Micron both address the trends in automotive connectivity and in-vehicle experience driven by advanced systems. QCOM discusses how wireless connectivity and digitalization transform the in-vehicle experience, while Micron details how autonomous driving, ADAS, and in-vehicle infotainment increase requirements for memory and storage. Both explicitly mention the role of 'cloud-connected' or 'car-to-cloud' platforms; QCOM notes car-to-cloud platforms gather vehicle analytics, and Micron highlights qualifying solutions for 'cloud-connected platforms' to power data-rich automotive services. They share the view that data-rich, intelligent automotive services are a primary growth driver.

sentences.text: Car-to-cloud platforms are designed to help automakers improve cost efficiencies, create new service opportunities throughout the lifecycle of a vehicle with over-the-air (OTA) update capabilities and gather valuable vehicle and usage analytics.
This is driving the development of a new architecture for the software-defined vehicle.

Automotive: Advancements in autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems, and in-vehicle infotainment systems continue to increase the requirements for high-performing memory and storage products, with higher reliability requirements for leading-edge products.

In 2024, we qualified our automotive LPDDR5X, UFS 3.1, and NOR flash storage solutions for a comprehensive set of cloud-connected platforms designed for power data-rich, intelligent automotive services.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA offers a scalable data center-based simulation solution, DRIVE Sim, for testing and validating self-driving platforms and developing digital cockpits, supporting a software-defined approach that enables over-the-air updates for continuous innovation throughout a vehicle's life.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and NVIDIA disclose that the automotive industry is shifting towards software-defined vehicle architectures enabled by digital cockpit transformation and over-the-air (OTA) update capabilities. QCOM highlights that digitalization and car-to-cloud platforms enable OTA updates to create new service opportunities, while NVIDIA explicitly describes its 'software-defined approach' as designed for continuous innovation via OTA updates throughout the vehicle's life. Both identify digital cockpit development and connected connectivity as key drivers, though QCOM focuses on the cockpit experience and connectivity infrastructure, while NVIDIA emphasizes the simulation and validation tools (DRIVE Sim) and end-to-end AI computing architecture supporting this shift.

sentences.text: Digitalization of the automotive cockpit including wireless connectivity continues to transform the in-vehicle experience, enabling greater personalization of content and settings for both drivers and passengers as automakers respond to growing interest from consumers to bring their digital lifestyles into the vehicle.

Car-to-cloud platforms are designed to help automakers improve cost efficiencies, create new service opportunities throughout the lifecycle of a vehicle with over-the-air (OTA) update capabilities and gather valuable vehicle and usage analytics.

In addition, we offer a scalable data center-based simulation solution, NVIDIA DRIVE Sim, based on NVIDIA Omniverse software, for digital cockpit development, as well as for testing and validating a self-driving platform.

Our unique end-to-end, software-defined approach is designed for continuous innovation and continuous development, enabling cars to receive over-the-air updates to add new features and capabilities throughout the life of a vehicle.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA leverages its AI technology leadership to deliver end-to-end automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing solutions under the DRIVE Hyperion brand, which includes high-performance computing hardware, sensor sets, and software platforms for autonomous driving and intelligent in-vehicle experiences.
comparisons.comparison: QCOM and NVIDIA both identify the in-vehicle cockpit and automated driving as core components of the modern automotive technology landscape. QCOM states that digitalization of the automotive cockpit transforms the in-vehicle experience, while NVIDIA defines its automotive market as comprising 'platform solutions for automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing.' Both companies leverage AI and advanced computing to power these experiences, with QCOM focusing on wireless connectivity and personalization, and NVIDIA providing the DRIVE Hyperion platform for AI-driven autonomous and intelligent cockpit experiences.

sentences.text: Digitalization of the automotive cockpit including wireless connectivity continues to transform the in-vehicle experience, enabling greater personalization of content and settings for both drivers and passengers as automakers respond to growing interest from consumers to bring their digital lifestyles into the vehicle.
Automotive market is comprised of platform solutions for automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing.

DRIVE Hyperion consists of the high-performance, energy efficient DRIVE AGX computing hardware, a reference sensor set that supports full self-driving capability as well as an open, modular DRIVE software platform for autonomous driving, mapping, and parking services, and intelligent in-vehicle experiences.
